instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you how to choose a strong photograph. For the reunion poster: mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's. Yours is a little blurred.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very observant. Pity we haven't reached the lesson about supporting a colleague. Will you at least send mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send them together, the same size. No favorites.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've learned fairness from someone, then. Put mine above his; that's just the order I taught you to lay out a page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to leave room in a plan. Keep Friday free; I may need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promised Alex I'd paint his kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you can make commitments now. Could you keep your phone on for me, at least?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. It'll be on silent while we're painting, but I'll check it. Which flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice to know my lessons have earned me a silent phone. Leave the sound on; this is just planning ahead.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to win that swimming medal. Now let the charity auction have it; you're ready to be known for something bigger.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only race I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you finally believe it counts. Good. You don't need the metal to keep the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it instead? I want people to see my name on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Present it to the buyer yourself. Use the clear voice we practised at prize-giving; nobody will miss whose medal it was.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember my lesson about spending on what you use? Sell the signed guitar and we can replace our fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature. I can't sell that night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're separating an experience from an object. The night stays yours; the guitar can buy us cold milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. Let me copy the concert date out of the lining first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case, then. You're finally spotting what matters. Let me photograph the guitar without it.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's investigate the broken vase. I taught you to notice small details; start with that open window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's glue on your fingers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good eye, finally. But don't stop at the first clue. I'll help you inspect the glue cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a piece of the vase stuck to your thumb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you've kept looking. Get the tweezers and I'll show you how to remove evidence without leaving your fingerprints on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office plant's dead. I taught you to investigate before blaming anyone; I'll help you work through it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with your coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent memory. Now move beyond observation, as we practised. I'll test whether the machine makes plant-safe coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You added six sugars. The machine didn't do that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've isolated a variable. I'll make the comparison cups; you label them. Put the sugar counts on, not my name.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into the garage with the cafe. Remember my lesson about making a useful morning of an errand? Let's have breakfast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're asking practical questions. Next one: does the breakfast include unlimited toast? I taught you to check that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The mechanic just texted. He wants to show me the dent before we eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Time you learned to delegate. You get us a table and order for two; give me the keys and I'll deal with his questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you open that rent letter, help me hang the curtains. I taught you to finish one job before starting another.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to read a deadline. Let's send him a picture of how well we're caring for his place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take one now and ask whether we're behind on rent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that crooked curtain in it. What did I teach you about a level line? Hold this end up; I'll keep your phone safe.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery couldn't sell your cake, but those roses show you're finally using the piping lesson I gave you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They called it inedible. I thought I had a talent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You do. Remember when I taught you display cakes? You've made one sturdy enough for a window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ring them and offer it for the window. Will you explain that part?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ring first. You're still learning how to present your work; I'll make sure they understand the roses before they mention the sponge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine sent your poem back because it's too large a voice for one page. I taught you to stop being timid, and look at you now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They said it wasn't suitable. If you think it's bad too, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally taking your work seriously. Now take my judgment seriously: they haven't got room for what you're doing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you put that on the cover if I print it myself? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Put my name under it; you've learned to make people stand behind their advice.
